items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: You know, I just did a thing on Sinatra.

ctx.x: You know, when he worked with Eddie Arnold, he only worked with Eddie Arnold. When he worked with Hank Snow, he only worked with Hank Snow. And then Elvis was one of the openers and I guess he saw him at one of those little airport things and — the guys didn’t get pissed off that the girls were in love with him. They said wow, I want to dress like that. I want to do something like that guy. He’s different than us. And we think we’re rocks and everything, but look at the style this guy’s got. And that’s unusual.…

times has that happened? You know? He was something. My people loved him. Oh my God. When he played Buffalo, you could hear the jewelry being put on by his Italian women, from blocks away. “I don’t care,” the wives would tell their husbands, “I don’t care, you’re getting me tickets to the Memorial Auditorium. I don’t care what it costs, you take out a loan. You’re out there with the boys drinking, you’re doing this, we’re going to see Frank or you ain’t getting sex for the next month.”
